verses.text: Gather together, yes, gather together, you shameful nation,
before the appointed time arrives and that day blows away like chaff, before the LORD's fierce anger comes on you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes on you.
Look for the LORD, all you humble people of the land, you who do what he commands. Look for what is right. Look for humility. Perhaps you will be protected on the day of the LORD's anger.
Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon will be left in ruins. Ashdod will be emptied at noon, and Ekron will be pulled up by the roots.
How terrible it will be for you who live by the sea, you people from Crete! The LORD's message is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you, and no one will be left."
The land by the sea will become pastures, with shelters for shepherds and pens for sheep.

That land will belong to the survivors of the people of Judah. There they will find pasture. In the evening they will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon. The LORD their God will take care of them and bring back their good fortune.
"I have heard the insults of Moab and the mocking of the Ammonites. They insulted my people and bragged that they would take their land.

So as surely as I live," says the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, "Moab will become like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah. They will become a place of weeds and salt pits, a wasteland forever. The survivors of my people will plunder them. Those left from my nation will take over their land."
This is what they will get for their pride, because they insulted and mocked the people of the LORD of Armies.
The LORD will be terrifying to them when he destroys all the gods of the earth. Then people from every nation, each in its own land, will worship him, even those living on distant shores.
"You people of Cush will also be killed by my sword."
He will reach out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria. He will leave Nineveh in ruins, as dry as the desert.

Flocks and herds will lie down there, and creatures of every kind. The desert owl and the screech owl will roost on the tops of its columns. Their calls will echo through the windows. Rubble will fill the doorways, and the cedar beams will be exposed.

This is the city that was so proud and felt so safe. She said to herself, "I am the one! There is no one else but me." What a ruin she has become, a place where wild animals rest! Everyone who passes by laughs and shakes their fist at her.
